terms.definition: The heat energy change measured at constant pressure.
terms.examiner: Standard conditions are 100 kPa and a stated temperature, usually 298 K.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change when one mole of a compound is formed from its elements, with all reactants and products in their standard states under standard conditions.
terms.examiner: One mole of the compound; from its elements; standard states. The value for an element in its standard state is zero.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change when one mole of a substance is burned completely in oxygen, with all reactants and products in their standard states under standard conditions.
The enthalpy change for a reaction is independent of the route taken.
terms.examiner: With formation data: products − reactants. With combustion data: reactants − products.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change needed to break one mole of a covalent bond, averaged over a range of different compounds.
terms.examiner: Values from mean bond enthalpies differ from experimental ones because the real bond enthalpy depends on the molecule, and the data refer to gases.

terms.definition: The energy needed to raise the temperature of 1 g of a substance by 1 K.
terms.examiner: In q = mcΔT, m is the mass of the liquid that is heated, not the mass of the solid added or the fuel burned.
